header.decision: Which roadmap feature to build in Q1
header.decision_check: The brief names two decisions: the Q1 roadmap pick and whether the Starter plan has a problem worth fixing. One survey should settle one decision, so this report takes the roadmap pick as the survey's decision (the MaxDiff in q5 was built for it) and reads the Starter results as evidence only. The cancellation survey below is designed to settle the Starter question on its own.

findings_summary.finding: Starter customers are much less likely to recommend: NPS -5.9 against 35.8 on Growth.
findings_summary.evidence: Difference -41.7 points, p <0.001, significant after adjustment (threshold 0.0125 for 4 segment tests).
findings_summary.decision: Treat Starter as the problem segment; the cancellation survey and calls focus there.

findings_summary.finding: 'Packages and memberships' and 'Waitlist that fills cancelled slots' lead the roadmap list, and they are a statistical tie.
findings_summary.evidence: Count scores 0.429 and 0.424, paired test p 0.902; the third item scores 0.099.
findings_summary.decision: Don't pick between the two from this survey alone. Fitness accounts score packages 0.527 against 0.393 elsewhere (exploratory, not a planned test), so ask which segment the Q1 plan serves.

findings_summary.finding: Price is the most common complaint in the open answers: 78 mentions, 32.6% (plus or minus 5.9) of those who wrote something, 59 of them from Starter.
findings_summary.evidence: Coded from 239 open answers; 0 fell under Other. 31 of the 78 came from detractors.
findings_summary.decision: Test it properly: the pricing question in this survey was double-barreled and can't separate price from support.

findings_summary.finding: Company NPS is 14.6 raw and 16.3 reweighted by plan, because Growth answered fewer than its share of accounts.
findings_summary.evidence: Growth is 31.8% of answers against 38.0% of accounts (-6.2 points). Raw range 6.9 to 22.3; weighted range 8.5 to 24.0 on an effective 336.9 answers.
findings_summary.decision: Report the weighted figure as the company NPS and show the raw one beside it. The two ranges overlap, so the reweighting changes the headline, not the story.

findings_summary.finding: 2 gaps that look like news are not proven: Business beats Growth by 11.0 NPS points (p 0.353), and promoter share runs from 34.1% (plus or minus 9.0, n 91) in Fitness to 45.7% (plus or minus 10.1, n 81) in Clinic across the 3 industries with 30 or more answers (chi-square p 0.298, df 2).
findings_summary.evidence: Business has 47 answers, so its NPS range is 27.4 to 66.2. Other has only 29 answers, so it is shown at 34.5% (range 19.9 to 52.7, n 29) and not tested.
findings_summary.decision: Don't plan around either. Reading Business alone at plus or minus 10 points needs about 73 answers from its 288 accounts; Other needs about 69 answers from its 240 accounts.

next_wave_fixes: Give the next wave one decision. The Starter question moves to the cancellation survey below.
Rewrite q2, q3 and q4 as in the question audit before the next wave.
Keep the MaxDiff, and add the fitness segment as a planned cut.
Business needs 73 answers for plus or minus 10 points. All 288 Business accounts were invited and 47 answered cleanly (16.3%), so the next wave needs a reminder and a personal ask to reach about 25%.

cancellation_survey_design.decision: Which cancellation cause to fix first in Q1: price on the Starter plan, a missing feature, or setup and sync problems

audience.source: Klaviyo segment 'Cancelled in the last 90 days'

sample_size.target: plus or minus 10 points at 95% confidence
sample_size.response_rate_basis: no past survey to cancelled accounts, so the planning rate is 10% and is stated as an assumption
sample_size.verdict: Short of the 77 needed even with every cancelled account invited. Read the shares as directional (about plus or minus 15 points), send one reminder after 4 days, and add 8 to 10 short calls with cancelled Starter accounts.

questions.text: What was the main reason you cancelled?
questions.type: single choice, options in random order, 'Other' last
options: A feature I needed was missing
It was hard to set up or use
I moved to another booking tool
questions.skip_logic: 'A feature I needed was missing' goes to c2; 'I moved to another booking tool' goes to c3; everyone else goes to c4. c2 and c3 then go to c4.
questions.bias_check: pass: neutral, one idea, covers the causes seen in the open answers plus 'Other'

questions.shown_if: c1 = A feature I needed was missing

questions.text: Which booking tool do you use now?
questions.shown_if: c1 = I moved to another booking tool
questions.bias_check: pass: 'Another tool' and 'I'd rather not say' close the gap the Q4 survey had

questions.text: Before you cancelled, did you contact our support team about it?
questions.bias_check: pass: past behaviour, not a prediction

questions.text: Is there anything else you'd like us to know? (optional)
questions.bias_check: pass: optional, so it can't push people to drop out

cancellation_survey_design.not_asked: Plan, tenure and industry come from the account data joined on the account id, so the survey doesn't ask them.
cancellation_survey_design.length: 5 questions, 3 seen by most people, about 2 minutes
